body:
Rewrote the router to safely delegate ANY flag-using or stdin invocation straight to real grep (turbogrep implements none of grep's real flag surface -- -i/-r/-n/-v/-c/-l/-A/-B/-C/-e/etc) -- only the exact bare 'grep PATTERN FILE...' shape is a turbogrep candidate, verified against real grep's -n line-numbering format too. Installed as ~/.local/bin/grep (real system-wide-for-this-account PATH override, no narrower 'Claude-Code-only' mechanism exists -- flagged explicitly to founder before installing, confirmed as an informed, deliberate tradeoff: 'its ok that its slower if its logging the data that will make turbogrep faster'). Real bug found on first actual invocation through the installed symlink: dirname on  doesn't resolve symlinks, so SCRIPT_DIR pointed at ~/.local/bin instead of PARENA/tools/, turbogrep binary not found, exit 127. Fixed with readlink -f. Verified working through the real installed symlink: bare pattern (turbogrep path) and -n flag (real grep fallback) both correct, both logged to NDJSON. Real finding, not fixed here: Claude Code's own Bash tool has a harness-injected 'grep' shell FUNCTION (routes to ugrep via the claude binary itself) that takes priority over any PATH override -- this router affects the account's other shells/scripts but not my own Bash tool's grep calls specifically, since bash resolves functions before PATH and this function isn't something I should try to override (core CLI internals, not a dotfile).

⚓ ☃
title: grep router installed at ~/.local/bin/grep -- flag-safe rewrite + symlink resolution fix
